messages: incident-bot: [2419004321] :rotating_light: Alert: spike in `cuda_illegal_memory_access` errors on infer-rt-prod (us-west2). Observed: 8 nodes with container restarts in last 3m, P99 latency +600ms. Pager routed to @sre-oncall. Elaine: ack. I’m on it — looking at node list and recent deploys. Tomas: quick note: we rolled nvidia-driver to 535.22 last night across us-west2-gpu pool. Could be related. Elaine: grabbing logs from one of the crashing pods. snippet: ``` [2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] runtime: cuda_illegal_memory_access at 0x7ffef3a0 stack: inference::kernel::dispatch -> device::pagewalk -> kvcache::apply container: infer-svc-7f9d5 (node=gpu-05) signal 11 (SIGSEGV) - misaligned address during pagewalk OOM not observed at container-level, kernel shows address fault ``` Maria: Our autoscaler did a scale-down ~14:05 which started pod evictions while a large batch load was ongoing. That could have created partial KV cache states and triggered pagewalks on freed memory. Elaine: interesting — logs show mixed stack: some look like genuine kernel pagewalk faults, others show repeated `cudaMemcpy` failing with illegal access. I’m increasing log level and capturing full dmesg from node. ops-bot: [14:18] customers_impacted: 37 orgs, ~4.8% of requests returned 5xx in last 12m. Top impacted: AcmeCorp (heavy embedding traffic). Tomas: can we cordon the most-suspect nodes and drain them gracefully? If it’s driver-level, a full node reboot may be needed. Elaine: cordoning gpu-05,gpu-09,gpu-12 now. `kubectl cordon gpu-05 && kubectl drain gpu-05 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m` Ken: on the traffic side — switching routing to fallback model variant to reduce GPU mem pressure. I’m flipping route policy: ``` redwood route set-policy --route infer-heavy --fallback redwood-slim-cpu --mode immediate ``` Elaine: applied canary: rerouted 30% of traffic to cpu fallback, latency increased but 5xx dropped for those requests. Good for customer mitigation. Tomas: can we also reduce batch sizes at runtime? If the pagewalk is triggered by large KV cache lookups mid-batch, smaller batches may avoid the race. Elaine: updating runtime config on dedic-pool-1: set `max_batch_tokens=1024` -> previous 8192. Pushing now. ops-bot: [14:31] node_restarts: gpu-05 restarted 3x in 10m; kernel logs include `NVIDIA: page-table walk failed, misaligned pte` entries. Maria: filing infra ticket to check last kernel modules and the NVidia driver ABI mismatch. Also tagging kernel-team — @Tomas please cross-check with the 535.22 release notes for known pagewalk bugs. Tomas: will do. Early glance: 535.22 mentions "improved pagewalk caching" but not regressions. Reaching out to vendor slack. Elaine: summary for now: mitigation = cordon/drain worst nodes, reduce batch size, route to CPU fallback for heavy customers, restart affected pods. Monitoring shows 5xx rate halved within 7m after changes. Ken: customer comms: drafting a short message for AcmeCorp + top 10 affected tenants. Copy below — please edit: "We observed transient 5xx errors on inference pipelines in us-west2 between 14:12–14:40 UTC. Mitigations applied (node drain, traffic reroute, batch-size reduction). If you saw errors, retry requests — no model data lost. Postmortem forthcoming." Elaine: LGTM. Add note that we applied CPU fallback for 30% traffic and are performing a gradual rollback of driver if vendor confirms regression. Tomas: vendor acknowledged receipt. They asked for full dmesg and kernel oops; I uploaded artifacts to their ticket (link: https://vendor.tickets/12345). ops-bot: [14:46] checkpoint: incident entered mitigation state. Severity -> Sev2. Elaine: handing off to Ken for next-hour remediation and follow-up with infra + vendor. Ken, items for you: - continue draining/isolating any nodes with repeated SIGSEGVs - coordinate driver rollback test on one node (gpu-21) in staging - ensure routing remains on fallback until we confirm stability - collect full coredumps and dmesg for postmortem attachment Ken: taking over. I’ll run a staged rollback to 534.x on gpu-21 in staging, then prod dry-run on gpu-07. If stable, plan mass rollback overnight (low traffic window). Elaine: thanks — leaving notes in incident doc: https://internal.re/redwood/incidents/2419004321. sre-oncall: oncall note: next check-in at 15:10 UTC. If error rate > baseline for 10m, escalate to infra-systems. Maria: opened infra bug: INFRA-2026 "gpu driver/pagewalk: investigate cuda_illegal_memory_access spikes" and attached logs. Ken: quick ask — do we want to enable a temporary retry policy in the edge gateway to smooth out client errors while we fix nodes? Elaine: yes — add 1 retry with jitter for 5xx on inference route for affected region. Ops, please apply. ops-bot: [14:58] change_applied: edge-retry-policy updated for us-west2. Elaine: final short status before handoff: mitigations effective, customer impact reduced from 4.8% -> 1.2%, ongoing infra investigation. Handoff complete. :thumbsup: Ken: acknowledged. I’ll own follow-ups and postmortem. Leaving this thread open for updates. incident-bot: [15:10] Reminder: scheduled check-in. Ken: (15:12) quick update after staging rollback test: node gpu-21 on 534.88 passed 30m soak with no illegal access events. Planning mass rollback tonight at 02:00 UTC unless vendor provides hotfix. Elaine: noted — adding to the postmortem checklist: timeline, config changes (batch_size decrease), routing changes (cpu fallback), node list drained, driver rollback plan, customer comms. Ken: thanks everyone. Action items assigned in ticket INFRA-2026 and incident doc.
